title: ‘Gen Z is a force that can’t be ignored’: Dharmendra Pradhan days after resignation
content: Former Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan acknowledged the immense potential of Gen Z, stating that grasping their hopes and dreams is essential for national advancement. He noted that the eagerness of young people surpasses any governmental duties, a point he shared with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who subsequently reached out to the youth. Pradhan maintained that prioritizing the nation's welfare is of utmost importance.

title: Captain of turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight may have failed dope test
content: During a turbulent flight from Phuket to Delhi, the captain of an Air India aircraft reportedly tested positive for psychoactive substances. The turbulence caused a significant scare, resulting in hospitalization for thirteen passengers and four crew members. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is conducting a detailed investigation, and the flight crew has been suspended from flying duties as per standard procedures.

title: Delhi woman crushed between vehicles; kin alleges Mercedes driver was drunk, speeding
content: A tragic incident unfolded when a 70-year-old woman lost her life after a Mercedes collided with her WagonR, causing it to crash into a parked vehicle. The driver of the Mercedes, identified as Subham Sharma, was detained at the scene. It has been reported that Sharma was coming back from a party, and a blood sample for testing was taken. Fortunately, the occupants of the WagonR only suffered minor injuries.

title: Watch: De Paul scores stunner, reveals Messi’s No. 10 jersey in emotional tribute
content: Rodrigo De Paul scored Inter Miami's opening goal with a spectacular long-range strike. He then revealed Lionel Messi's iconic number ten jersey beneath his own shirt. This emotional tribute honored his close friend, who was absent from the match. Messi missed the game after the passing of his father, Jorge Messi, at sixty-eight. De Paul's gesture offered a powerful message of support to his grieving friend.

title: Elon Musk says Starship Flight 13 recovery ‘not looking good’ after splashdown
content: SpaceX's Starship recovery is struggling against the tumultuous waters of the Indian Ocean, with Elon Musk admitting the situation appears grim. Despite these difficulties, engineers managed to capture invaluable images of essential spacecraft components. This visual data is expected to contribute significantly to enhancements in Starship design and its reusability. Notably, the mission marked SpaceX's most successful Starship test flight to date.

title: The Stateless Kings: How Chess preserves an ideal in a fractured world
content: Aarav Dengla traces the journeys of chess players caught between their game and the politics of their countries. From Viktor Korchnoi’s defection from the Soviet Union to Alireza Firouzja’s break with Iran and Ian Nepomniachtchi playing under the FIDE flag after opposing Russia’s war, he explores how FIDE has stood between players and geopolitical upheavals, providing a neutral ground for those who could no longer compete under their national flags. For these stateless kings, the banner did not erase identity - it protected their freedom to play.

title: Government spending on education below Unesco's 15% standard
content: India's education funding aligns with GDP standards but falls short of public spending goals. Completion rates for secondary schools lag behind national and UNESCO guidelines. This funding pattern emerges as countries shift focus from education financial targets. India's extensive education initiatives benefit millions of students, yet the sector continues to grapple with persistent challenges despite increased program deployment.

title: Michael Dell’s son’s startup offers $695 alternative to costly home generators
content: Zach Dell's Base Power is installing home battery systems across America.  These systems offer backup power and reduce electricity bills for customers.  The company aims to replace expensive gas generators with its innovative technology.  Base Power is rapidly expanding its operations and customer base nationwide.  This startup is valued at thirteen billion dollars after significant funding.

title: India’s markets have strong domestic cushion, but global risks loom: Sebi
content: India's economy is poised for substantial growth in 2026-27, driven by strong domestic demand and increased government spending. While this positive outlook is promising, external factors such as the ongoing Middle East conflict and fluctuating oil prices present significant risks. Additionally, last year saw a historic exodus of foreign investment from Indian equities, but favorable domestic conditions may help mitigate these global challenges.

title: Virginia teen uses AI and CRISPR to boost biofuel from microalgae
content: Fourteen-year-old Millie Pradawong has developed an AI-powered computational tool that predicts how CRISPR gene editing could improve microalgae for biofuel production. Her project, MACRO, aims to increase oil production without reducing algae growth. A finalist in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge, Millie hopes her work will support future research in clean energy and biotechnology.

title: Mark Zuckerberg gave an update on ‘Meta's 4 am layoff email’ to employees
content: During an earnings call, Meta's CEO highlighted the difficult decision to lay off 8,000 employees, which is integral to a transformative AI-focused restructuring plan. While costs related to compensation and infrastructure continue to escalate, the company boasts strong revenue performance. Meta's proactive investments in AI infrastructure are poised to usher in new employment opportunities in an evolving digital ecosystem.

title: Pakistan cricketers face ban after playing in ‘unsanctioned’ Zambia T20 league
content: A potential two-year ban looms for former Pakistan cricketers who participated in an unauthorised Zambian league. The Pakistan Cricket Board has reacted strongly, emphasising that all players must obtain proper approvals before playing. Reports suggest that some cricketers encountered significant troubles regarding payments and accommodation during the tournament. This serious matter unfolds as the ICC intensifies its scrutiny on global franchise cricket activities.

title: Colombia rocked by car bomb blast a day after new President takes charge
content: In southwestern Colombia, a car bomb detonated at a toll plaza on Saturday, just a day after Abelardo de la Espriella took office as president. The army promptly attributed the incident to dissident FARC factions, leaving two security guards injured. In response, President de la Espriella issued a stern warning to armed groups, urging them to comply with the rule of law.

title: LeBron James’ wife Savannah reveals why Hermès saleswoman turned her away
content: Savannah James opened up about an alleged Hermès shopping dispute in Italy, claiming a saleswoman was fired after she and April McDaniel were reportedly turned away despite having an appointment. The friends later described how the store addressed the situation. Savannah also discussed marriage, motherhood and life alongside LeBron James, stressing the importance of staying grounded, authentic and invested in a relationship despite the pressure of public life.

title: Patrick Mahomes’ million-dollar collection: Cars, watches, mansions and more
content: Beyond the gridiron, Patrick Mahomes is crafting a formidable business empire. His strategic investments in sports franchises and innovative tech firms underscore his savvy approach to entrepreneurship. Coupled with lucrative endorsements from major global brands, Mahomes enjoys a life adorned with exotic cars, high-end watches, and luxurious homes. This multifaceted portfolio highlights his ambition and keen sense for success in business.

title: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry hit $100 million milestone with foundation
content: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry's foundation Eat. Learn. Play has marked a major $100 milion investment after helping changing lives for close to a decade.

title: Wing Commander arrested for spying after being ‘honey-trapped’ by Pak operatives
content: A Wing Commander in the Indian Air Force is currently under serious accusations of leaking critical defense information. It is reported that he fell victim to a honey trap orchestrated by operatives from Pakistani intelligence using social media. Allegations suggest he secretly installed software designed to steal data on a colleague's device. Prior to his arrest by the Delhi Police, he was under close scrutiny by the IAF.

title: FIFA hits back at ‘concerted effort’ to undermine Infantino amid fresh allegations
content: FIFA has come out in staunch defense of president Gianni Infantino, rebutting fresh allegations and widespread criticism. The organisation has accused unnamed detractors of orchestrating a campaign aimed at destabilising its leadership. While UEFA acknowledged a severance payment to a former employee associated with Infantino, he continues to enjoy robust support from various continental federations despite European discontent.

title: Vance calls PM after US Senate passes 100% tariff bill, discusses boosting ties
content: On Saturday, VP JD Vance engaged in a conversation with PM Narendra Modi, reiterating both nations' dedication to strengthen partnerships in vital sectors such as trade, defense, and upcoming technologies. They shared insights on international matters of shared concern, coinciding with the US Senate's approval of a bill focused on Russian oil transactions.

title: Latest Arunachal map shows 3 places illegally held by China
content: India has finalized its official mapping of the contested frontier areas of Arunachal Pradesh, encompassing crucial sites such as Asaphila and Maja. In response, the People's Liberation Army of China has erected various structures and roadways in these disputed territories. Historical conflicts have marked this sensitive border, and this mapping initiative effectively bolsters India's stance regarding the ongoing territorial dispute.

title: Jadeja’s Kuldeep imitation leaves Gambhir in splits - Watch
content: Ravindra Jadeja entertained teammates by mimicking Kuldeep Yadav’s bowling action, leaving Gautam Gambhir laughing during India’s Colombo warm-up match. Devdutt Padikkal impressed with an unbeaten 142, boosting his chances for the opening Test. Jadeja scored 63 and Manav Suthar added 41 as India reached 357/6. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel disappointed, managing just two and one respectively.

title: Jana Nayagan day 17: Thalapathy Vijay film sees 135% jump, earns Rs 2.35 cr
content: Thalapathy Vijay's latest venture, 'Jana Nayagan,' has experienced a remarkable surge at the box office, raking in Rs 2.35 crore in India on its seventeenth day. This impressive figure marks a notable improvement from the previous day's revenue. Notably, the Tamil version has been pivotal in driving the movie's domestic success. Overall, the film has surpassed Rs 312 crore globally, showcasing its widespread appeal.

title: US rejects China’s attempt to enforce new restrictions at Scarborough Reef
content: The United States has firmly rejected China's maneuvers at Scarborough Reef, asserting that Beijing's environmental assertions are hindering Filipino fishermen from accessing their traditional fishing grounds. As a staunch ally in the Indo-Pacific, Washington stands in solidarity with the Philippines, highlighting China's contentious approach of using legal claims to assert maritime rights. This reaffirmation underscores US commitment to its allied nation's interests amidst complex maritime disputes.

title: Proposed MDR for UPI transactions will be nominal, says government
content: The government has pledged that the upcoming UPI merchant discount rate will be minimal. This fee will be applicable only to certain merchants and transactions that surpass a designated threshold. Importantly, person-to-person UPI payments will remain free for all users. This initiative is designed to enhance the sustainability of India’s digital payment ecosystem and facilitate service expansion into rural and semi-urban regions.

title: Iran says deal on Strait of Hormuz is close but not enough to open the waterway
content: A significant shipping route agreement is nearing completion between Iran and Oman, which is essential for reviving the strategic Strait of Hormuz. Iran insists on receiving US compensation and an end to hostilities as part of the deal. Meanwhile, the UAE has noted that another ship has been attacked in the strait, highlighting that normal oil trade can only commence once these larger issues are resolved.

title: IN-SPACe moves to privatise operations of Rs 986 cr spaceport
content: IN-SPACe is actively on the lookout for private partners to operate Isro's new small satellite launch complex located in Tamil Nadu. This innovative facility is expected to streamline small rocket launches and improve operational efficiency. The chosen operator will oversee all functional aspects, while Isro commits to providing technical training and guidelines during a specified duration. The initiative aims to elevate India's capabilities in small satellite launches.

title: Kanimozhi slams Vijay’s all-party delimitation meet as ‘political drama’
content: Political discord reigns in Tamil Nadu over a significant meeting regarding delimitation. The DMK has labeled the event a theatrical display aimed at diverting public focus, while AIADMK raises doubts about the chief minister's sudden urgency. Additionally, several parties are advocating for constitutional protections in lieu of simple verbal commitments, striving to maintain the current Lok Sabha seat allocations in the state.

title: India 'playing Hasina card', says Bangladesh home minister
content: Bangladesh has openly criticized India for allegedly exploiting the Hasina card, which presents a challenge to India's aims of fostering amicable relations with Bangladesh. The home minister emphasized the importance of mutual respect and sovereignty between nations, expressing concerns that Hasina may be colluding with external forces against the current government. India's frequent gestures toward Hasina are deemed unwelcome by some, complicating neighborly ties.

title: Trump forces US oil billionaire to exit Venezuela
content: The Trump administration is ramping up its efforts to persuade Harry Sargeant III to withdraw from Venezuela. In a significant move, the Treasury Department has frozen the assets of his offshore company connected to oil operations. This halt enables Sargeant to divest from the Venezuelan entity effectively, a role he previously held as a crucial facilitator between Washington and Caracas, while ensuring compliance with US foreign policy.

title: Government appoints 30 judges to high courts of Calcutta, MP, Karnataka, Madras
content: The law ministry notified thirty new judges for four high courts on Saturday. Madras High Court received fifteen appointments, while Calcutta got eight and Karnataka six. Judicial officers and advocates were elevated to the benches, with most appointed as additional judges. Over sixty lakh cases are pending across India's twenty-five high courts. The law minister cited collegium delays for the significant number of vacancies.

title: Agni-4 fills key gaps in India's missile arsenal, strengthens China deterrence
content: India successfully tested its Agni-4 medium-range ballistic missile last Thursday.  This missile bridges a critical gap in India's strategic deterrence capabilities.  The Agni-4 missile can carry nuclear and conventional payloads with a 4,000 km range.  It features an advanced heat shield and a precise guidance system for accuracy.  This successful test reaffirms India's commitment to national defense technologies.

title: Trump shoots from Senate shoulders to punish Russia, by making India and China pay
content: The US Senate approved a bill allowing President Trump to impose tariffs. This legislation targets nations buying Russian oil and gas, including India. India faces potential 100% tariffs for its energy purchases from Russia. The bill grants the president discretion and includes exemption provisions for allies. This move could impact global energy markets and US consumers significantly.

title: 6 years after NDA exit, Punjab's SAD backs delimitation push
content: Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal now supports the women's reservation law rollout.  This move signals the government's potential revival of the Constitution amendment bill.  The government is also seeking support from DMK and NCP(SP) for the measure.  The bill aims to increase Lok Sabha's strength by fifty percent.  Its timing remains uncertain as lawmakers consider summoning Parliament.

title: EPFO, officers' body contest claims about new IT system
content: The rollout of EPFO's new IT system has resulted in a substantial backlog of claim issues. Field officials are grappling with an increasing number of pending auto claims, which have lingered for over twenty days and are causing significant discomfort to members. EPFO admits that this surge in pendency is a short-term effect of the system transition, although it was executed with minimal disruption to services.

title: Captain moves crew to citadel, thwarts pirate assault on India-bound vessel
content: In a daring move, the Indian Navy successfully thwarted a pirate assault on the Golden Arsenal in the perilous Gulf of Aden. The ship’s crew effectively sought refuge within an impregnable citadel that the invaders could not penetrate. Currently, four vessels remain under the control of Somali pirates, with Indian nationals on three of them.

title: Raids in four Kashmir districts in anti-national narrative case
content: On Saturday, Counter Intelligence Kashmir executed raids at five locations spread across the districts of Baramulla, Bandipora, Anantnag, and Shopian. During these operations, several electronic and digital storage devices were confiscated as part of an investigation into an anti-national narrative. As of now, no arrests have been reported in relation to this ongoing case.

title: Two memorials of 1962 war heroes figure in 27 places formally named in Arunachal
content: The Union government has formally named twenty-seven locations in Arunachal Pradesh. These places include memorials honoring Indian Army war heroes from past conflicts. Havildar Shere Thapa and Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat are among those recognized for bravery. Several strategically important mountain passes and a logistics hub were also officially identified. This action pays homage to soldiers who sacrificed their lives defending India's borders.

title: Rijiju, Rahul trade barbs over women's quota bill rollout
content: Union minister Kiren Rijiju called on LoP Rahul Gandhi to back the women's reservation bill during their exchange. In response, Rahul Gandhi noted that the 2023 bill had already received unanimous approval. He raised concerns about the holdup in implementing the legislation and its connection to the delimitation process. Gandhi insisted on prompt action to enforce the 2023 law, underscoring the heated political discourse on women's empowerment.

title: Restore J&K statehood, says human rights forum
content: An advocacy group for human rights calls for the restoration of statehood and the repeal of the 2019 Reorganisation Act. They argue that statehood should not be contingent upon the regional security situation. The forum additionally demands statehood for Ladakh and its inclusion in the Sixth Schedule. Their report highlights police inadequacies despite court mandates on detentions and brings attention to the injustices faced by Kashmiris after acts of terrorism.

title: Science min dedicates to nation first-of-its-kind ‘eco-educational hub’ in Lucknow
content: Union science minister Jitendra Singh launched the CSIR-NBRI eco-educational hub in Lucknow, a dynamic facility focusing on environmental education and the conservation of biodiversity. The hub includes an enlightening heritage trail that highlights India's botanical heritage and a specialised Bamboosteum that showcases various uses of bamboo. Moreover, attendees witnessed the introduction of a new herbal formulation designed to support male reproductive health.

title: Scientists uncover the aluminium shield helping a tiny crustacean survive
content: In a groundbreaking discovery, scientists have identified a deep-sea crustacean, the amphipod Hirondellea gigas, which uses aluminum to survive in the Mariana Trench, one of Earth's most extreme environments. Its unique aluminum-coated exoskeleton helps resist calcium dissolution under immense pressure, allowing it to thrive where life was previously deemed impossible. This remarkable adaptation showcases innovative survival mechanisms in the deep ocean.
